AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
A Detailed Accident Report(DAR) was filed on 10.07.2019 by the Investigating Officer.

The said DAR was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 11.01.2019 at about 11:00 AM in which Sh.
Amit Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Vrikesh (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained injuries.

As per petition, at the relevant date and time, he was going to office on his motorcycle bearing no.
DL-8SBW-7453 from his house.

When he reached over the Wazirabad Flyover at about 11:00 AM,

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

15 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2023.12.15 16:51:44 +0530 was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust Amit Kumar(I)(Fir 59/19 Ps Timarpur) vs Sandeep Kumar (The Oriental Insurance ... on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173435053/
9 manner.

(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.
Although, the petitioner has not placed on record any original medical bills but a pragmatic view is required to be taken considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner.

It is Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

Petitioner would have naturally incurred considerable expenses for his treatment.
Petitioner has averred that he has incurred about Rs.1,00,000/- on his treatment and the expenditure is still continuing for his continuous treatment.
Therefore, keeping in view the nature of injuries, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 19.
As per MLC, doctor gave the opinion that as per records, the nature of injury seems grievous.
In chargesheet, R-1 namely Sandeep Kumar was challaned u/s. 279/338 IPC.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the pain and sufferings which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.25,000/- is liable to be awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10. As already discussed above, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.
Petitioner claimed compensation on account of special pecuniary damage relating to treatment,
hospitalization, medicine, transportation, diet, loss of earning during the period, he was injured, loss of earning during the period of treatment, future medical expenses,
non- pecuniary damages, damages for pain suffering and trauma, loss of expectation of life alongwith interest.
The copies of FIR,
Chargesheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, MLC,
Seizure Memos of R-1 also corroborate the testimony of PW1.
Further, mere a discrepancy in the registration number of the vehicle in DAR and FIR is not sufficient to disburse the version of the petitioner which is otherwise reliable.
12. In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, he was going to office on his motorcycle bearing no. DL-8SBW-7453 from his house and when he reached over the Wazirabad Flyover at about 11:00 AM, then suddenly &
abruptly offending vehicle being driven by its R-1, at a terrible speed, rashly and negligently, in a zig-zag manner, in complete contravention of traffic rules and regulations, without any indicator turned to his left and in the process hit him, as a result of this forceful impact, he fell down on the road.
The same is duly substantiated by the site plan.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the PANKAJ Date:
 SHARMA 2023.12.15  16:51:36  +0530 offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending Amit Kumar(I)(Fir 59/19 Ps Timarpur) vs Sandeep Kumar (The Oriental Insurance ... on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173435053/
8 vehicle at the relevant time.
15 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2023.12.15 16:51:41 +0530 but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2023.12.15 16:51:44 +0530 was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust Amit Kumar(I)(Fir 59/19 Ps Timarpur) vs Sandeep Kumar (The Oriental Insurance ... on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173435053/
9 manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
17.
In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.
Although, the petitioner has not placed on record any original medical bills but a pragmatic view is required to be taken considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the pain and sufferings which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
In the absence of any corroborative material supporting the claim of the petitioner as to his employment or his monthly earnings, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to a matriculate person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
The maturity amounts of the FDR(s) be credit by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the petitioner(s) near the place of their residence.
